xuejiang-sp-group-tip: Special-effect parameters for the chart named "今年も「雪降り、メリクリ」目指して頑張ります！！.100.SP" (the effect is forced on by the file name)
baoying-sp-group-tip: (Test) UI sprite parameters for the chart named "Retribution~CycleofRedemption~.100.SP" (the effect is forced on by the file name; sprites come from the RetriSP resource pack)
resolution-tip:
Width x height of the video
Render time roughly scales with the pixel count, so this saves the most time
fps-tip:
Frame rate of the video
Higher looks smoother and renders slower
hw-accel-tips: Use GPU encoding for better performance
hevc-tips: Use HEVC encoding, which has higher compression rate and slower speed
video-encoder-tip:
Video encoder handed to ffmpeg
nvenc / qsv / amf / vaapi are the hardware encoders of NVIDIA / Intel / AMD / Linux, much faster than CPU
When the hardware is unavailable rendering fails outright; you can pin a working encoder name on the Settings page
encoder-list: Compatibility - AVC/H.264,High Compression - HEVC/H.265,Fast - MPEG4 (Not Recommended)
sample-count-tips:
Must be a power of 2. A non-1 sample count enables MSAA Anti-Aliasing
Forced off while "Motion Trail" is on: the trails do not go through the multisampled buffer
fxaa-tips: FXAA, as a low-cost anti-aliasing method, will cause the picture to be blurred, and it is not recommended to turn it on
bitrate-crf-tip: Range 1-51, the smaller the value, the higher the quality
output-ref-0:
Reference:
-Small File Size - Discord etc.
  Resolution: 720P
  Encoder: HEVC,
  Quality: 40
  (Click to apply)
output-ref-1:
Reference:
-High Quality - Bilibili etc.
  Resolution: 1600P
  FPS: 120
  Encoder: HEVC,
  Quality: 24
  Lossless Audio: On
  (Click to apply)
aggressive-chart-tips: Hide off-screen notes, improve rendering speed, but may cause some charts to display incorrectly
aggressive-note-tips: Hide overlapping notes, improve rendering speed, but may cause some notes to disappear
aggressive-particle-tips: Hide overlapping particles, improve rendering speed, but may cause some particles to display incorrectly
speed-tip:
Chart speed multiplier (default 1)
Chart and music are played at the same multiplier, and the video length follows
ending-length-tip:
Extra seconds rendered after the chart ends (default 0)
Leaves a short tail of empty footage
render-loading-tip:
Render the official loading screen at the start of the video (the part with the illustration / title / difficulty colors)
On adds a few seconds to the head; off starts right at the chart (default off)
chart-debug-line-tip: Debug text size of judge line (a gear appears once it is above 0, where you pick the fields to show)
chart-debug-line-field-ulp-tip: Appends a warning when the speed is so high that float precision runs out (yellow past 1px, red past 10px)
chart-debug-line-field-kind-tip: Content of text / image / GIF / paint lines
chart-debug-line-field-rot-tip: Rotation of the judge line this frame, in degrees
chart-debug-note-tip: Debug text size of note (a gear appears once it is above 0, where you pick the fields to show)
chart-debug-note-field-angle-tip: Rotation of the judge line this frame, in degrees
xuejiang-sp-burst-combo-tip: The second stage of the effect starts here: the difficulty text switches, and the score rolls back to the real value within the window
xuejiang-sp-fake-notes-tip: The faked score is combo ÷ this count × total score; with 305, 4 combo = 0013115 and 238 combo = 0780328
xuejiang-sp-fake-bar-seconds-tip: Seconds the faked progress bar takes to fill at a constant rate, as if the chart were that long; with 120 the reveal combo sits around 0.72
xuejiang-sp-roll-scale-tip: Rollback window = gap between the two notes at the reveal combo × this scale; 1 means it ends when the next note is judged
xuejiang-sp-volume-percentile-tip: Loudness percentile of the whole track that fills the bar (0~1); too low keeps the bar full, too high keeps it thin
xuejiang-sp-volume-gamma-tip: Loudness is raised to this power before drawing; 1 = linear (bar stays above 0.8), 2 = squared
xuejiang-sp-volume-smooth-tip: Time constant (seconds) of the volume bar; smaller follows the music closer, larger moves less
xuejiang-sp-diff-fake-tip: Difficulty text shown at bottom right during the faked stage
xuejiang-sp-diff-real-tip: Difficulty text shown at bottom right after the reveal
xuejiang-sp-face-hit-start-tip: Hit time (s) of the first round that swaps the combo counter for a face; this is note 1888
xuejiang-sp-face-period-tip: Interval between the four face rounds (s); 16 beats at 234 BPM
xuejiang-sp-face-rounds-tip: How many rounds swap the combo counter for a face; 0 disables it
xuejiang-sp-face-lead-show-tip: Seconds before each hit that the "shown" face appears (3.5897)
xuejiang-sp-face-lead-roll-tip: Seconds before each hit that the "rolling" face appears (2.8205); must be smaller than the value above
xuejiang-sp-face-text-show-tip: Text shown at the combo position while the note just appeared
xuejiang-sp-face-text-roll-tip: Text shown at the combo position once the note starts rolling
xuejiang-sp-face-text-hit-tip: Text shown at the combo position when the note is judged
baoying-sp-wow-height-tip: Height of the WOW! sprite at the top left
baoying-sp-wow-offset-x-tip: Move the WOW! sprite to the right
baoying-sp-title-height-tip: Height of the song-title sprite at the bottom left
baoying-sp-title-offset-x-tip: Move the song-title sprite to the right
baoying-sp-score-offset-x-tip: Move the score to the right
baoying-sp-score-height-tip: Height of one score digit at the top right
baoying-sp-score-gap-tip: Spacing between score digits at the top right
baoying-sp-score-squeeze-tip: Horizontal squeeze of score digits (1 keeps the original ratio)
baoying-sp-combo-offset-x-tip: Move the combo number to the right
baoying-sp-combo-height-tip: Height of one combo digit at the top center
baoying-sp-combo-gap-tip: Spacing between combo digits at the top center
baoying-sp-combo-label-height-tip: Height of the COMBO sprite under the combo number
baoying-sp-combo-label-offset-x-tip: Move the COMBO sprite to the right
baoying-sp-combo-label-offset-tip: Spacing between the COMBO sprite and the combo number
baoying-sp-diff-height-tip: Height of the SP LV.? sprites at the bottom right
baoying-sp-diff-gap-sp-lv-tip: Spacing between the SP and LV. sprites
baoying-sp-diff-gap-lv-question-tip: Spacing between the LV. and ? sprites
baoying-sp-diff-squeeze-tip: Horizontal squeeze of the difficulty sprites
baoying-sp-diff-offset-x-tip: Move the difficulty sprites to the right
baoying-sp-digits-rtl-tip: Lay out score and combo digits from right to left (that is how the game writes them)
baoying-sp-hit-fx-scale-tip: Scale of the hit-effect sprite (0 keeps the value from the resource pack)
baoying-sp-hit-fx-rotate-tip: Rotate the hit-effect sprite with the judge line (the game keeps it upright, so this is off by default)
baoying-sp-particle-count-tip: Number of hit particles (0 draws no particles)
judge-mode-tip:
Default: auto play always judges Perfect
Force Good / Force Bad: every note is judged as that result
watermark-tip: Small translucent text centered at the bottom of the screen; empty draws nothing
roman-tip:
Score / combo / result numbers use Roman numerals
When both this and "Chinese Mode" are on, Roman wins
chinese-tip:
Score / combo / result numbers use Chinese numerals
When both this and "Roman Mode" are on, Roman wins
multi-lang-gate-tip: Tick to show the Roman Mode / Chinese Mode switches below. This only shows or hides them; it does not change any render setting.
combo-tip:
The small line below the combo count (default AUTOPLAY)
Anything reading as COMBO (including look-alike glyphs) or longer than 50 chars is shown as AUTOPLAY instead
Empty draws nothing
difficulty-tip:
Difficulty shown in the color block on the right of the loading screen
Empty takes the number from the chart's "Difficulty Text"
Only appears while "Loading Screen" is on
judgeOffset-tip:
Offset of the judgement moment in milliseconds (default 0)
A positive value delays judgement and hit effects, negative advances them
file-name-format-tip:
supports variables (use the real field name; * is not a wildcard):
 %date%   date YYYY-MM-DD
 %time%   time HH-MM-SS
 %file%   source file name without extension
 %level_prefix%   difficulty prefix (e.g. IN)
 %info.xxx%   chart info, replace xxx with a field name, e.g. %info.name%, %info.charter%
 %config.xxx%   render config, replace xxx with a field name, e.g. %config.fps%, %config.resolution%
unknown variables are kept as-is
render-line-extra-tips:
A judge line can also be a text / image / GIF / paint line (RPE extended events)
Turned off, those non-normal judge lines are not drawn at all
Normal judge lines and notes are unaffected (default on)
render-ui-level-tip:
Which text goes in the difficulty slot
On: the full difficulty text including the level (e.g. IN Lv.15.6)
Off: only the difficulty tier (e.g. IN)
Requires the difficulty switch above
render-ui-bar-tip: The chart progress bar at the very top of the screen (with a white marker on the right)
render-background-tip:
Whether to draw the illustration background
Off leaves a plain black screen
background-dim-tip:
Opacity of the black overlay on the background (0~1)
1 = fully darkened, 0 = none
overrides the same setting in chart info
default 0.1
preserve-framebuffer-tips:
Keeps every rendered frame on screen:
each frame paints the previous frame back over the whole screen and draws the current one on top, so no history is ever dropped and the trails keep growing.
Mutually exclusive with "Background": an opaque full-screen image covers the trails.
While it is on, anti-aliasing is forced off: the trails live in a single-sampled accumulation buffer, which MSAA cannot see.
render-particle-square-tip:
The ring of square shards flying out of hit effects
Off leaves the rest of the hit effect only (default on)
pure-config-chart-tip:
Flattens every judge line's move / rotate / disappear / speed events, keeping only each note's horizontal screen position — what is left on screen is the chart's configuration.
The chart file is never modified — the conversion happens at render time, and judgement timing stays exactly as before (default off)
pure-config-chart-line-y-tip:
Every judge line is pinned to this horizontal line: 0 = bottom edge, 1 = top edge, 0.5 = middle.
The reference implementation uses 0.1 (near the bottom edge)
pure-config-chart-speed-tip:
Note fall speed and hold tail length both use it; tap / drag / flick stay at 1.
Invisible holds that used speed 999 in the chart become visible in this mode
pure-config-chart-side-lines-tip:
Notes that are close to vertical at judge time go to two vertical judge lines at the left and right edges, leaving only horizontal notes on the middle line.
Those lines judge as well: their notes fall from the middle of the screen outwards (on by default)
pure-config-chart-side-x-tip: Distance from a vertical judge line to the nearest screen edge: 0.5 = centre, 0.1 = a tenth in from the edge
pure-config-chart-angle-tip:
How many degrees a note's angle at judge time may differ from horizontal and still stay on the middle line.
Notes outside that range go to the two vertical lines by the direction they fall: the left half-circle (-90~90, 0 = left, 90 = up) to the left line, the right half-circle (90~270, 180 = right, -90 = 270 = down) to the right one, swapped for notes on the lower side of the line; their height on the line is their original Y coordinate; 45 by default, i.e. -45~45 and 135~225
pure-config-chart-noise-tip:
Notes that are inside a block area at judge time get a block area rectangle drawn around them (the same look as inverted force position, but only on those notes).
The chart's own block area layer is not drawn in this mode (once the judge lines are flattened it no longer lines up with the picture); the rectangle size and the two time windows are controlled by the four settings below instead of Render -> Block Area -> Force Position (on by default)
pure-config-chart-noise-height-tip: Full height of the rectangle as a fraction of screen height: 0.1 is a tenth of the screen
pure-config-chart-noise-width-tip: Half width as a fraction of screen height (divided by 10): 1.1 matches the default judge range
pure-config-chart-noise-time-tip: The rectangle only shows once a note is within this many seconds of its judge time
pure-config-chart-noise-delay-tip: How long the rectangle lingers after the note has been judged
fixed-lane-chart-tip:
(Test) Flattens the whole chart onto one horizontal base line plus a set of fixed lanes: every note lands on a lane's x position at its judge time and still falls vertically
Sides alternate, so consecutive notes go left, right, left, and both hands carry the same load
Notes that share a judge time (doubles, triples) are handled as one group and packed into one hand first; only what does not fit spills to the other hand
Each side runs from the index lane outward through the middle finger to the ring finger (three lanes); inner lanes come first and a note only moves outward while the inner lane is still too recent
A note only switches to the other hand when all three lanes on its own side are full; with the third lane off the ring lane is skipped and leftovers stack on the nearest lane of that side
Flick and Drag are always pinned to the centre lane (x = 0); every other note type goes to a side lane
This mode draws no block areas and no judge range
Every chart becomes the same key layout, handy for practice or for comparing charts
fixed-lane-gap-tip: Distance between neighbouring lanes as a fraction of the screen width: 0.14 means 14% of the screen width
fixed-lane-speed-tip: Multiplier for the falling speed: the bigger it is, the faster notes fall (the line height and hold tails use it too)
fixed-lane-line-y-tip: Where the base judge line sits: 0 is the bottom edge, 1 the top edge, 0.5 the middle
fixed-lane-interval-tip: Minimum seconds between two notes on the same lane (holds count by their tail); a note that comes too soon moves one lane outward, or stacks on the nearest lane of its side when the third lane is off
fixed-lane-hold-length-tip: Draw the hold body with its original length; turn it off to keep only a short stub above the head, which looks like a tap while judging stays the same
fixed-lane-third-tip: Whether to bring in one extra lane per side when the usual two per side are full; turning it off lets notes overlap on the nearest usual lane
play-split-view-tip:
Opens two windows side by side when playing: the left one shows the original chart, the right one shows the reworked chart (only for Pure Config / Fixed Lane charts)
The main chart drives the clock, so pausing it pauses the side chart too
The side window stays silent; audio only comes from the main window
render-extra-tips:
Whether to load the chart's own extra.json / extra1.json
That file holds custom shader effects (Effect / global Effect) and video attaches
Turned off, extra.json is not read, and with 1x sampling outside low-resolution mode the offscreen render target is skipped as well (default on)
block-area-spark-tip:
The flowing spark layer inside the full block area noise.
Turning it off removes only the sparks; fill / edge / glow and the scene snapshot stay untouched.
(The simplified block area never had sparks. On by default.)
block-area-hover-tip:
While a finger is pressed on the block area, a glow lights up at that spot and stays until you let go; notes in that area cannot be hit (official rule: the block area is a no-touch zone)
Only touches made during an active block area are blocked
Only shows where the block area covers; turning this off hides the glow but the area still blocks touches
Driven by real touches: appears in play and preview only, not in autoplay renders
block-area-hover-radius-tip:
Radius of the glow, 0.5 in the official game.
Bigger values light up a wider area; 0 draws nothing.
block-area-noise-blotch-tip:
The noise blotch layer blended into the fill colour.
Turning it off leaves a clean flat fill; edge / glow / scene snapshot stay untouched.
(On by default.)
block-area-displace-strength-tip:
How far the noise pushes the sampling coordinates. Upstream value: 0.15.
0 = no distortion at all; larger values twist the scene snapshot inside the block area harder.
(Full block area only.)
block-area-pixel-scale-tip:
Pixel granularity of the scene snapshot. Upstream value: 6.
Larger = coarser pixels; 1 = no pixelation.
(Full block area only.)
block-area-displace-speed-tip:
How fast the noise flows across the block area. Upstream value: 1.5.
Larger = more restless; 0 = completely static.
(Full block area only.)
block-area-noise-radius-tip:
Sampling radius of the noise texture. Upstream value: 0.48.
Larger = bigger blobs.
(Full block area only.)
block-area-noise-smoothness-tip:
Smoothness of the noise texture. Upstream value: 1.
Smaller = harder grains and sharper edges.
(Full block area only.)
block-area-edge-noise-tip:
Strength of the jagged fringe along the block area's edge. Upstream value: 1.
When the mask is composed every texel shifts its sampling coordinate by the noise texture — that displacement is the only source of the jagged edge.
0 = clean straight-edged rectangle; 1 = upstream look.
(Full block area only.)
simplified-block-area-tips:
Fills the block's own rectangles with a flat colour — no noise, no edge, no spark
Light red before enable, red after enable (off by default)
simplified-block-area-text-tip:
Prints the block's index (starting from 1) at the centre of each simplified block:
pale before enable, the text colour after enable (default #FF6094)
(both colours are configurable below; requires Simplified Block Area, off by default)
block-area-reuse-tip:
Treats block areas that share the same geometry, subtract flag and animation keyframe shape
(only their 4 times differ) as ONE block area appearing many times; they share a single index,
so a chart's block-area count drops dramatically
(the chart format has no index field, so indices can only follow first-appearance order)
The picture is pixel-identical - every window still appears and disappears on its own times
The only change is the number printed by Simplified Block Area Text: "which entry" becomes
"which block area" (requires Simplified Block Area + Simplified Block Area Text, off by default)
block-area-lava-tip:
Replaces the full block area's fill with two Minecraft textures (netherrock / lava):
a block that has not started yet (appear~enable) shows netherrock, the active phase and
the fade-out after it show lava
Lava plays its 16 frames at 160ms each, all blocks sharing one clock
The texture is anchored to the screen, one cell per 1/16 of the screen height, so it slides
underneath a block that moves or scales
Only real blocks are textured: subtract (hollowing) blocks and the ones synthesised by
Forced Positioning keep their plain colour
While it is on, Noise Blotch / Block Area Distortion / Block Area Spark have no effect
(the engine ignores them and never rewrites the values you saved) so the textures stay clean (only applies while Simplified Block Area is off; off by default)
water-screen-tip: Cover the whole screen with a Minecraft water texture (above judge lines, notes and UI) and enable the note HP system: any note drawn on screen keeps losing HP, and 0 HP is judged as a MISS even in AUTOPLAY. Off by default.
water-opacity-tip: Opacity of the water layer (0~1). Default 0.5
water-flow-speed-tip: Downward scrolling speed of the texture, in screen-heights per second; 0 = still. Default 0.15
water-cell-scale-tip: One cell is screenHeight / this value. Default 16 (1/16 of the screen height)
water-drown-delay-tip: How long a note must stay in the water (on screen) before it starts losing HP. Default 1 second; 0 means it starts draining immediately
water-damage-tip: HP lost on each damage tick while the note is on screen. Default 1
water-damage-interval-tip: How many seconds between two damage ticks. Default 1 second
water-death-time-tip: How long the red / tilted / fading death animation lasts before the note disappears (seconds). Default 0.5
water-death-particles-tip: Number of white particles spawned when a note dies. Default 8
water-sfx-volume-tip: Volume (0~1) of the hurt / death sounds, picked randomly from the hit folder. Default 0.5
water-sfx-max-tip: How many hurt / death sounds may play at the same time (1~512, default 500, effectively unlimited)
ui-level-tip: Interface level: higher levels reveal more windows and options. This only affects this UI; hidden options still render with their current values.
direct-block-hollow-tip:
Hides the hollowing blocks (subtract blocks) in the simplified block area
and restores what they cover straight from the frame below,
still drawing the merged outer outline (off by default)
block-area-force-position-tip:
Ignores the chart's own block areas (works on charts that have none): covers the whole screen
with one always-enabled block area and cuts a rectangle out around every note, giving
"block area everywhere except the notes"
Holds get the hole at the head of their bar, other notes at their centre; fake notes get none
(height/width are the two fields below; requires Block Area, off by default)
block-area-force-height-tip:
Rectangle height = this value x screen height
Default 0.2 (= 20% of the screen height)
block-area-force-width-tip:
Rectangle half width = this value x (screen height / 10), the same basis as Judge Range Width
Default 1.9 (about the judge range width)
block-area-force-show-tip:
Also draws the cut-out rectangles themselves, so you can check where the holes are
Colour and opacity reuse the Judge Range settings (off by default; with it on you only see the holes)
block-area-force-time-tip:
Time window for the holes, in seconds (default 3): only notes whose judgement is already within this many seconds carve a hole
Notes still far from their judgement get covered by the block area again
How long a hole survives after the judgement is set by Forced Hole Delay
block-area-force-delay-tip:
After a note is judged, its hole lingers for this many seconds (default 0.3) before the block area covers it again
For holds the judgement counts to the end of the bar, so the hole stays while you hold it and this long after you let go
0 means the hole is covered the moment the note is judged
block-area-force-invert-tip:
Draws the Forced Positioning rectangles themselves as block areas and leaves the rest of the screen bare
That is "block area only around the notes", the opposite of the default "block area everywhere except the notes"
Requires Forced Positioning; the rectangles carry no block area number (off by default)
render-judge-range-tips:
The strip perpendicular to the judge line
Half width = Judge Range Width x (screen height / 10) (Tap / Hold and Flick / Drag have one field each, same unit)
Length = Judge Range Length x screen width (default 5.0, i.e. 5x the screen width)
Fades in from the "Judge Range Appear Time" (default 3s) before the judgement
render-double-hint-tip:
Two notes at the same moment are enlarged and drawn differently so a double hit is easy to see
Off draws doubles like any other note (default on)
render-pending-note-tip:
Tints the note that will be judged next
The nearest one only (simultaneous notes all change colour)
Drawn above the block area, so the noise never covers it
Redrawn by the note's own drawing code, so rotation, movement and hold bodies match exactly
pending-note-color-tip: Colour used to tint the next note, in hex (e.g. #FF2E2E); leave empty for the default red
dynamic-bitrate-control-tip:
On: encode by quality parameter (CRF / CQ / QP), bitrate follows the picture complexity; the field below holds the quality value
Off: encode at a fixed bitrate (-b:v); the field below holds the target bitrate
Default on
max-particles-tip:
The maximum number of hit effects that can be displayed at the same time.
Low 5000, Medium 25000, High 200000
render-start-time-tip:
Second of the music to start rendering from (0 = from the beginning)
Everything before it is neither drawn nor mixed into the audio
render-end-time-tip:
Second of the music to stop rendering at
Empty = render to the end of the audio
fade-tip:
1.0 unit size (half the screen)
Positive numbers hide on top,
Negative numbers hide on bottom
bg-blurriness-tip:
Gaussian blur radius of the background image (default 80)
0 = no blur, larger is blurrier; only applies while the background is on
alpha-tint-tip:
Tint Note based on different alpha:
(0.0, 0.5] Blue,
(0.5, 1.0) Red
judge-range-time-tip:
When the judge range first shows up: how many seconds before a key's judgement it starts to be drawn (default 1.0).
Beyond that it is not drawn at all.
It reaches "Judge Range Opacity" at (appear time - fade duration) before the judgement.
judge-range-alpha-tip:
Alpha (0~1) the judge range is drawn with:
0.1 = 90% transparency (very faint)
Fades in from the "Appear Time", reaching it at (appear time - fade duration)
judge-range-transition-tip:
How long the fade-in takes (default 0.7, upstream: 1.2s):
Between "appear time before the judgement" and "appear time - this value before" the range goes from 100% transparent to 90% transparent (alpha 0 -> 0.1).
The value it settles at comes from "Judge Range Opacity".
judge-range-width-tip:
Tap / Hold only (Flick / Drag use the next field).
Half width = this x (screen height / 10). Upstream: 1.9.
At 1920x1080 that is about 205px half width. Lower it to make the white bar narrower.
judge-range-width-flick-tip:
Same unit as the previous field: half width = this x (screen height / 10).
Default 2.1, only slightly wider than Tap / Hold's 1.9. (A Flick's red-key match judgement is +/-2.1 world units, but that is the hit test, not this display width.)
judge-range-noise-occlusion-tip:
On: where the noise field overlaps, the judge range fades out and yields to it (upstream behaviour).
Off: the judge range is drawn on top of the noise as usual.
No effect while the noise field itself is off.
judge-range-length-tip:
Length of the judge range along the judgement direction, in units of the screen width (the screen width is a constant 2.0 in world coordinates).
Default 5.0 = 5x the screen width; since that is far taller than the screen it always spans the whole screen.
judge-range-color-tip:
HEX color, e.g. #FFFFFF
Empty means the default white #FFFFFF
block-area-alpha-tip:
Alpha (0~1) the simplified block area is filled with:
1 = fully opaque; below 1 the fill is see-through and an
opaque merged outline is drawn around it
(that outline ignores this value)
block-area-normal-color-tip:
HEX color, e.g. #E51A1A
Color of the normal (full) block area
Only its hue is used to rotate the official palette, so the
light/dark layering stays as the original
Default red #E51A1A means unchanged
block-area-color-tip:
HEX color, e.g. #E51A1A
Fill color of the simplified block area **after** `enable`
Empty means the default red #E51A1A
simplified-block-area-text-color-tip:
HEX color, e.g. #FF6094
Color of the simplified block index **after** `enable`
Defaults to #FF6094 (1 / 0.3765 / 0.5804)
Empty means the default value
simplified-block-area-text-pale-color: Simplified Block Area Text Pale Color
simplified-block-area-text-pale-color-ti:
HEX color, e.g. #FFFFFF
Color of the simplified block index **before** `enable`
Defaults to white #FFFFFF
Empty means the default value
block-area-density-tip:
How fine the pixel grains along the block edge are (default 2.5):
higher makes the grain cells smaller, the edge thinner and denser
and closer to the block outline;
lower makes the cells bigger and the edge thicker and sparser
(only affects the edge grains, not the size or position of the block)
block-area-distort-tip:
When off the block area stops distorting: the fill displacement and the jagged edge noise are both zeroed,
so a block area is just "solid colour / scene snapshot x opacity" with clean straight edges.
Grain (pixel scale), spark, blotch, edge and glow each keep their own switch. On by default = official look
